newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Rugby League board outlines peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Australian Rugby League board outlines peace talks.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL) board said on Wednesday it would pursue talks with Rupert Murdoch's Super League and television companies in an effort to establish a united national competition in 1998.

ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker said the board would aim for a two-tier system, with a "sustainable" number of teams in the national league, and a state-based competitions open to all existing ARL clubs.
However, if agreement could not be reached the ARL would go ahead with its Optus Cup competition in 1998, he said.
"We have a strong competition in the Optus Cup and we are more than able to go ahead with that competition in 1998," Whittaker said.
"In the meantime, we are giving everyone in the game a chance to work for an even more positive solution.

Whittaker has met recently with Ian Frykberg, director of sport at News Ltd, the Australian arm of Murdoch's News Corp, which divided the sport when it set up the 10-team Super League this year for pay-television viewing.
Whittaker said Super League was keen to ensure it recovered the money invested to start up the rival league after a protacted legal battle.
Both the ARL and Super League have long acknowledged that rugby league can only sustain one national league in the long-term.
Other sticking points are likely to include which side would have administrative control of a single national league, and the number of teams in the competition.
